description:
Read who can do what in a module: who can open it, run each activity, see each field and table column, and see each listing.

- `access` holds one entry per item that has rules; an item that is absent is open to everyone with module access. Each entry is a rule ("everyone" / "nobody") or allow/deny lists of grantees: "guest", {member: username}, {profile: people module}, or {profileField, profile, in: [values]} — the position grant, e.g. Position = Manager. Change them with set_module_access; an entry can be edited and sent back as read.
- Each entry carries the server's `summary` of who gets in: relay it rather than working the rules out yourself. `legacy` lists rules the vocabulary cannot express (obsolete listing grants among them); `warnings` flags grants that match no one, stale option values and similar.
- `other` lists rules that belong to no current item: deleted activities or fields, print templates, actions.
- `options` lists the people modules and the fields a grant can name, with their values, and each people module's `unlinkedMembers`: the members with no entry there yet (add them with submit_activities, Username = their username). `targets` lists the activity, field and listing names that can be protected.
- `listingDefinitions` lists every listing as save_listing takes it (id, name, filters in the list_entries dialect, columns, bound activities, read-only flags).

Only platform administrators bypass these rules; workspace admins are subject to them.

workspaceId.description: Workspace ID for this call. The MCP keeps no workspace between calls, so pass it every time; omit only when INISTATE_WORKSPACE_ID is configured.

name: get_module_access
